title: Ashes in the Blue Hour
intent: A self-contained late-night noir jazz meditation whose quiet weight comes from low-register baritone counterlines, sparse felt-piano harmony, and a slow blues pulse.

tempo.feel: Slow 12/8 blues pulse with brushed triplets, spacious phrasing, and broad breathing pauses.

tonality.mode: minor blues with flat-five coloration, suspended dominants, and long pedal tones

instrumentation.name: felt piano
instrumentation.role: Sparse harmonic punctuation and opening atmosphere
instrumentation.timbre: Muted, soft-edged, widely spaced voicings with restrained pedal resonance

instrumentation.name: baritone saxophone
instrumentation.role: Low sustained counterlines and dark melodic shadow
instrumentation.timbre: Distant, breathy, warm, and subdued rather than forceful

instrumentation.name: upright bass
instrumentation.role: Quiet pedal anchor and occasional low connective movement
instrumentation.timbre: Round, woody, softly bowed or lightly plucked

instrumentation.name: brush kit
instrumentation.role: Subtle 12/8 pulse and gentle triplet motion
instrumentation.timbre: Whispered brushes with minimal cymbal brightness

structure.direction: Felt piano offers sparse minor-blues chords in open space; distant baritone saxophone enters with long, low tones.
Upright bass joins as a quiet pedal anchor while brushes establish soft triplets; baritone and piano overlap in restrained counterpoint.
Low-register lines become slightly denser and more interwoven, using flat-five tension and suspended dominants without increasing volume or becoming dramatic.
Brushes and bass recede first; baritone leaves a final breath-like phrase over a sparse felt-piano chord, ending hushed and unresolved.

production: Intimate acoustic quartet recording in a dim, softly reverberant room. Keep dynamics restrained, with close felt-piano detail, warm low-end separation, distant baritone depth, gentle stereo width, and a softened final decay.
assumptions: Target tempo set near 52 BPM to support the slow 12/8 pulse.
No fixed tonic chosen; the harmony remains deliberately veiled and pedal-oriented.
lyriaPrompt: Late-night noir jazz meditation for relaxation, approximately 120 seconds. Instrumental only, no vocals. Slow 12/8 minor blues pulse around 52 BPM, with brushed triplets, broad breathing spaces, and restrained dynamics. Begin with sparse felt-piano chords and a distant, breathy baritone saxophone playing low sustained counterlines. Add warm upright bass as a quiet pedal anchor, then whispering brushes. Develop overlapping low-register baritone and piano lines using flat-five color, suspended dominants, and long pedal tones; increase density subtly without getting louder or dramatic. [Intro] spacious piano and distant baritone. [Development] bass and brushes enter, forming a hushed blues undercurrent. [Climax] gently interwoven low-register lines. [Outro] remove brushes and bass, leaving a final breath-like baritone phrase over a sparse unresolved piano chord. Intimate acoustic room, soft reverberation, warm low end, tactile felt-piano detail, and a deliberately softened ending. Avoid bright production, fast swing, flashy solos, harsh cymbals, abrupt drops, vocals, and cinematic bombast.
